mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate decline below 5.0% indicates accelerating labor market strength, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months when UNRATE falls below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates robust aggregate demand, driving sustained equity market gains over 60 trading days through earnings momentum.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST and RSAFS growth fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth above 105.0 (INDPRO) during manufacturing capacity expansion signals improved supply chain efficiency, reducing input costs and boosting corporate margins for positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods of INDPRO above 105.0, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase above 2.0% signals rising inflation, triggering Federal Reserve tightening expectations that depress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) consistently indicate strengthening labor market conditions, supporting consumer spending and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle demand overheating (RSAFS > 450,000 and HOUST > 1,150) signals potential Fed intervention, causing short-term equity market pullbacks and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods where RSAFS > 450,000 and HOUST > 1,150, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent industrial production (INDPRO) growth and labor market expansion (PAYEMS) indicate robust manufacturing sector activity, driving short-term equity gains through earnings acceleration within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of INDPRO and PAYEMS growth fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances.
